offer.payment_plan_terms: The prospect asked for $1,000/month for six months on autopay against a business credit card. The rep first offered third-party financing (declined, because it would not qualify as a deductible business expense), then quoted $1,200/month for six months — a $7,200 total. When the prospect refused the $200/month premium and proposed delaying to mid-July, the rep improvised a three-month entry at $4,000, payable $2,000 immediately and $2,000 the following month, with the $4,000 verbally credited toward the $6,000 six-month price and a $2,000 top-up after three months. $2,000 was charged on the call. The renewal beyond six months was quoted as "only going to be like additional 3K for the next six months".
offer.guarantee_mentioned: "we guarantee your results... you have a baseline of a kettlebell that you start with... it could be, I don't know, 12 kilos. So the guarantee is that after six months, you will add at least eight kilos to your starting baseline." The rep separately conceded "With three months, you maybe not be able to see the full transformation."

Counter-evidence: the document he signed states a three-month programme — "it says terms, duration, program, last three months" — not the six months he believes he has bought
Counter-evidence: he twice asked for the six-month top-up to be put in writing and never received it
outcome.next_step: Second $2,000 charge next month; onboarding Zoom with Trevor on Tuesday 16 June at 4:15pm ET; prospect to complete the onboarding form and buy a single kettlebell before that call.

notable.note: Closed, but on a structure that exists nowhere in the price list: a three-month $4,000 contract carrying a verbal-only promise that it credits toward a $6,000 six-month total. The prospect signed unread and asked twice for the top-up in writing; the rep answered "you have my word on this. The calls are recorded." Separately, he disclosed lumbar epidural injections four years ago and a physician's instruction about what training to do, and was moved into loaded kettlebell work without anyone asking whether a clinician had cleared it. The rep also discussed peptide protocols ("then we can dial in the peptides"), shared his personal WhatsApp number, and signed off with an off-colour remark about who the prospect should share it with.
